mainTopic: Practical life advice, then whether the blood of a slaughtered animal is covered on שבת and יום טוב
overview: This amud opens with practical life advice. Raising sheep makes a person rich, and רבי יוחנן warns that lukewarm water is harmful, a warning the גמרא narrows step by step. רבי יוחנן then lists three sure ways to waste an inheritance, and רב עוירא learns from a פסוק how to spend on food, clothing and family. Next, רב עינא teaches that someone who slaughters for a sick person on שבת must cover the blood. רבה rejects this using רבי יוסי's ברייתא about a כוי, which rests on a קל וחומר from מילה. The קל וחומר is attacked twice, by the case of שופר and by רבי אלעזר הקפר. Still, its starting assumption shows that covering the blood does not override שבת, even after a permitted slaughter. Finally, the גמרא returns to the שופר answer and asks what kind of doubt it means, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Raising sheep and goats makes a person rich
steps.stepSummary: Someone who wants to become wealthy should raise small animals like sheep and goats.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who wants to become wealthy should go into raising small domesticated animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives practical financial advice: raising sheep and goats is a good way to become wealthy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a piece of everyday wisdom, not a הלכה about what is allowed or forbidden. The very next step will bring a פסוק to back it up.

keyTerms.meaning: small domesticated animals: sheep and goats

phrases.english: One who wishes to become wealthy
should engage in raising small domesticated animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this section with a piece of practical advice that continues the advice in the lines before it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Raising sheep and goats brings wealth.

steps.title: A פסוק shows that sheep enrich their owners
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא reads the word עשתרות in the פסוק as a hint to מעשרות, meaning that the flocks 'make rich' their owners.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: What does the פסוק mean when it says 'and the flocks of your sheep'? It means that sheep make their owners rich.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא brings a פסוק to support the advice from step 1. He uses a word-play on the פסוק's word for flocks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word עשתרות sounds like מעשרות, 'they make rich.' So the תורה itself hints that sheep bring wealth. That backs up the advice in step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the meaning of what is written

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said
What is the meaning of that which is written
"And the flocks of your sheep"
phrases.notes: דברים 7:13. The word עשתרות sounds like מעשרות, 'they make rich.'

phrases.english: that they enrich their owners.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a פסוק as support for the advice in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: The advice that raising sheep brings wealth.

steps.title: Lukewarm water is worse than a witch's cup
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says it is better to drink from a cup that may have witchcraft in it than to drink lukewarm water.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: Better a cup of witches than a cup of lukewarm water.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a health warning: lukewarm water is very unhealthy, even more dangerous than a witch's cup.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He makes the point sharp by comparison: even something we fear, like witchcraft, is better than lukewarm water. The next steps will narrow down exactly when this warning applies.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said
Better a cup of witches
phrases.notes: He means a cup that might have witchcraft in it. Even that is better than what comes next.

phrases.english: and not a cup of lukewarm water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new piece of practical advice from רבי יוחנן, this time about health.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Drinking lukewarm water is very harmful, worse than a cup that may have witchcraft in it.

steps.title: The warning applies only to metal vessels
steps.stepSummary: The danger of lukewarm water applies only when it was in a metal vessel. In a clay vessel there is no problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies only to metal vessels. In clay vessels, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to narrow רבי יוחנן's warning. The danger applies only to lukewarm water in metal vessels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the first of three limits. Water warmed in a clay vessel is not included in the warning, so the rule is smaller than it first sounded.

keyTerms.meaning: we have no problem with it

phrases.english: And this applies only in metal vessels
but in earthenware vessels
we have no problem with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the warning from step 3 to metal vessels only.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lukewarm water is harmful only if it was in a metal vessel.

steps.title: Even in metal, added spices remove the danger
steps.stepSummary: Even with metal vessels, the warning applies only when no spices were put into the water.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even with metal vessels, we said it only when he did not put spices into them. But if he put spices into them, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the warning a second time. If spices were added to the water, even in a metal vessel, there is no danger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a limit built on the previous limit. The danger now needs both a metal vessel and water with no spices in it.

phrases.english: And even in metal vessels
we said it only
where he did not cast flavorings into them
but if he cast flavorings into them
we have no problem with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second limit on top of the metal-vessel limit in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lukewarm water in a metal vessel is harmful only if no spices were added.

steps.title: Even without spices, boiled water is safe
steps.stepSummary: Even with no spices added, the warning applies only to water that was not first boiled.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even when he did not put spices into them, we said it only when the water was not boiled. But if it was boiled, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the warning a third and final time. Water that was boiled and then cooled to lukewarm is not dangerous.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After all three limits, the danger is quite narrow. It applies only to lukewarm water in a metal vessel, with no spices, that was never boiled.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's warning about lukewarm water ends up narrow. It applies only to metal vessels, with no spices added, and water that was never boiled.
steps.confusionAlert: The opening word וכי here means 'and even when,' not a question. Each line adds another limit to the warning; none of them argues with it.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי לָא שָׁדֵי בְּהוּ צִיבַיָּא נָמֵי
phrases.english: And even when he did not cast flavorings into them
we said it only where it was not boiled
but if it was boiled, we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי לָא שָׁדֵי בְּהוּ צִיבַיָּא נָמֵי לָא אֲמַרַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the third and last limit, finishing the narrowing of the warning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lukewarm water is harmful only if it was never boiled, in addition to the earlier limits.

steps.title: Three ways to waste an inheritance
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says, half-jokingly, that someone who wants to lose his inheritance should wear linen, use glass dishes, and hire workers without watching them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: Someone whose father left him money and who wants to lose it should wear linen clothes, use glass dishes, and hire workers and not sit with them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן lists three habits that quickly burn through money. He is warning people to avoid them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording sounds like advice, but it is really a warning: anyone who does these things will lose his money. The next step explains what kind of linen, glass and workers he means.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said
One whose father left him money
and he wants to lose it
phrases.notes: Said with a wink. Nobody wants to lose money; this is a list of what to avoid.

phrases.english: should wear linen garments
and should use glass vessels
and should hire workers and not sit with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִי שֶׁהִנִּיחַ לוֹ אָבִיו מָעוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new piece of practical advice from רבי יוחנן, now about managing money.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Linen clothes, glass dishes, and unsupervised workers quickly use up a person's money.

steps.title: Which linen, which glass, which workers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains each of the three: Roman linen, white glass, and workers with oxen.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Wear linen' means Roman linen. 'Use glass' means white glass. 'Hire workers and do not sit with them' means workers with oxen, who can cause a lot of damage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back over רבי יוחנן's three items and says exactly which case each one means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every linen, glass or worker wastes money. Only Roman linen, white glass, and unsupervised workers using oxen do, since oxen can do a lot of damage if nobody watches them.

phrases.english: He should wear linen garments
this refers to Roman linen.
And he should use glass vessels
this refers to white glass.
And he should hire workers and not sit with them
this refers to oxen, whose damage is great.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines exactly which case each item in step 7 refers to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three money-wasters are Roman linen, white glass, and unsupervised workers using oxen.

steps.title: Spend less on yourself, more on your family
steps.stepSummary: רב עוירא explains a פסוק in תהלים: eat below your means, dress at your means, and honor your wife and children above your means, trusting in הקב״ה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עוירא taught, sometimes in the name of רבי אמי and sometimes in the name of רבי אסי: What does the פסוק 'Good is the man who is gracious and lends, who orders his affairs with justice' mean? A person should always eat and drink less than he can afford, dress according to what he can afford, and honor his wife and children more than he can afford. They depend on him, and he depends on the One who spoke and the world came into being.
steps.whatsHappening: רב עוירא uses a פסוק to teach how to spend money wisely. There are three levels: below your means, at your means, and above your means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Orders his affairs with justice' is read as spending in the right measure for each need. Food is below your means, clothing matches your means, and your family gets more than your means. Spending above your means on family makes sense because they rely on him, and he can rely on הקב״ה to provide.

keyTerms.meaning: orders his affairs with justice / in proper measure
the One who spoke and the world came into being: הקב״ה

steps.whatToRemember: Eat below your means, dress at your means, and honor your family above your means. Your family depends on you, and you depend on הקב״ה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known guide for running a Jewish home: being careful with spending on oneself while being generous toward one's wife and children.

phrases.english: Rav Avira expounded

phrases.aramaic: זִימְנִין אָמַר לַהּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַמֵּי
phrases.english: sometimes he said it in the name of Rabbi Ami

phrases.aramaic: וְזִימְנִין אָמַר לַהּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַסִּי
phrases.english: and sometimes he said it in the name of Rabbi Asi
What is the meaning of that which is written
"Good is the man who is gracious and lends
who orders his affairs with justice"?
A person should always eat and drink
less than what he has
and dress and cover himself according to what he has
and honor his wife and children
more than what he has
for they depend on him

phrases.aramaic: וְהוּא תָּלוּי בְּמִי שֶׁאָמַר וְהָיָה הָעוֹלָם.
phrases.english: and he depends on the One who spoke and the world came into being.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ רַב עַוִּירָא זִימְנִין אָמַר לַהּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of handling money wisely, now based on a פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Spend below your means on food and drink, at your means on clothing, and above your means on honoring your wife and children.

steps.title: רב עינא: Slaughtering for a sick person on שבת requires covering the blood
steps.stepSummary: רב עינא publicly teaches that if someone slaughters a bird or wild animal for a sick person on שבת, he must cover its blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עינא taught at the entrance to the house of the ראש גלותא: Someone who slaughters for a sick person on שבת is obligated to cover the blood.
steps.whatsHappening: רב עינא gives a public ruling: when slaughtering on שבת is allowed for a sick person, the מצוה of כיסוי הדם still applies, even on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slaughtering is allowed here because of the sick person's danger. רב עינא adds that covering the blood comes along with it. That is a new claim, because covering is a separate act from the slaughter that saves the sick person.

keyTerms.meaning: The Exilarch, the head of the Jews in בבל
A sick person; here, one in danger, for whom שבת may be pushed aside
To cover the blood of a slaughtered bird or wild animal (כיסוי הדם)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two acts. Everyone agrees that slaughtering for the sick person is allowed. The question is only whether the extra act of covering the blood is also done on שבת.

phrases.english: Rav Eina taught publicly
at the entrance of the house of the Exilarch:
One who slaughters for a sick person on Shabbat
phrases.notes: He means a wild animal or bird, the kinds whose blood needs covering.

phrases.english: is obligated to cover the blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ רַב עֵינָא אַפִּתְחָא דְּבֵי רֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about covering blood on שבת and יום טוב, tied to the משנה's law of the כוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who slaughters for a sick person on שבת must cover the blood.

steps.title: רבה rejects רב עינא's ruling using רבי יוסי's ברייתא about a כוי
steps.stepSummary: רבה calls רב עינא's statement astonishing and says his interpreter should be removed. His source is רבי יוסי's ברייתא: a כוי is not slaughtered on יום טוב, and if it was, its blood is not covered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to them: He is saying something astonishing. Remove his interpreter from before him. For it is taught: רבי יוסי says, a כוי may not be slaughtered on יום טוב, and if one slaughtered it, its blood is not covered.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה strongly attacks רב עינא's ruling and brings a ברייתא of רבי יוסי as his source. The ברייתא's reasoning, explained in the next step, is what proves רב עינא wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי holds that even a doubtful covering, like the blood of a כוי, is not done on יום טוב. As the next step shows, his reasoning is built on the idea that covering never pushes aside שבת. That directly contradicts רב עינא, who said to cover on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: The interpreter who repeated the lecturer's words out loud to the crowd
An animal of doubtful status; it is unclear whether it counts as a wild animal (whose blood is covered) or a domestic one

phrases.english: Rabba said to them:
He is saying an astonishing thing;
let them remove his interpreter from before him,
for it is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Yosei says:

phrases.aramaic: כּוֹי אֵין שׁוֹחֲטִין אוֹתוֹ בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: A koy may not be slaughtered on a Festival,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם שְׁחָטוֹ אֵין מְכַסִּין אֶת דָּמוֹ.
phrases.english: and if one slaughtered it, its blood is not covered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly attacks רב עינא's ruling from step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב עינא's ruling that covering the blood is required on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי's ruling about a כוי rests on the idea that covering never pushes aside שבת, so covering on שבת cannot be required.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's קל וחומר from מילה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי argues: מילה pushes aside שבת when it is certain, yet a doubtful מילה does not push aside יום טוב. Covering does not push aside שבת even when it is certain, so surely a doubtful covering does not push aside יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: This comes from a קל וחומר: If מילה, which pushes aside שבת when it is certain, still does not push aside יום טוב when it is doubtful, then covering the blood, which does not push aside שבת even when certain, surely does not push aside יום טוב when doubtful.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives רבי יוסי's source: a קל וחומר comparing covering the blood to מילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מילה is the 'stronger' מצוה, since a certain מילה is done even on שבת, and still a doubtful one waits until after יום טוב. Covering is 'weaker', since even a certain covering is not done on שבת, so a doubtful covering, like a כוי, should certainly wait. Notice the premise that a certain covering does not push aside שבת. That premise is exactly what disproves רב עינא.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument: if a strong case has a limit, a weaker case surely has it too

steps.whyThisMatters: The premise inside this קל וחומר, that even a certain covering does not override שבת, is the real basis for רבה's rejection of רב עינא.

phrases.english: This is derived from an a fortiori argument:
If circumcision, whose definite obligation overrides Shabbat,
yet its uncertain obligation does not override a Festival,
then covering the blood, whose definite obligation does not override Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין דִּין שֶׁאֵין סְפֵקוֹ דּוֹחֶה יוֹם טוֹב?
phrases.english: is it not logical that its uncertain obligation does not override a Festival?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִקַּל וָחוֹמֶר וּמָה מִילָה שֶׁוַּדָּאָהּ דּוֹחֶה שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רבי יוסי's ruling quoted in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוסי's ruling that a כוי's blood is not covered on יום טוב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from מילה, which assumes that covering does not override שבת even when certain.

steps.title: The שופר case breaks the קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer that blowing שופר outside the מקדש disproves the pattern: a certain שופר blowing does not push aside שבת, yet a doubtful one does push aside יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Blowing the שופר in the provinces proves otherwise. Even a certain obligation to blow does not override שבת, yet a doubtful one overrides יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים attack רבי יוסי's קל וחומר with a counterexample: blowing שופר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's logic was: a מצוה that does not override שבת even when certain will surely not override יום טוב when doubtful. שופר fits the first half, since it is not blown on שבת outside the מקדש. Yet it breaks the second half, since a doubtful שופר is blown on יום טוב. So the pattern does not hold.

keyTerms.meaning: Blowing the שופר on ראש השנה
The provinces, any place outside the מקדש
Will prove, a counterexample that disproves the argument

phrases.english: They said to him:
Sounding the shofar in the provinces will prove otherwise,
phrases.notes: Outside the מקדש, the שופר is not blown when ראש השנה falls on שבת.

phrases.english: for its definite obligation does not override Shabbat,
and yet its uncertain obligation overrides a Festival!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ תְּקִיעַת שׁוֹפָר בִּגְבוּלִים תּוֹכִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the קל וחומר of step 12 with a counterexample.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The קל וחומר's general pattern from certain-and-שבת to doubtful-and-יום טוב.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: שופר is a case that does not override שבת when certain, yet does override יום טוב when doubtful.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר הקפר: מילה is different because it is not done at night
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר הקפר attacks the קל וחומר differently: מילה is weaker in one way, since it is not done on the nights of יום טוב. Covering applies at night too, so it may be stronger.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר הקפר the distinguished gave a refutation: What about מילה? It is special because it does not apply on the nights of יום טוב. Can you say the same about covering the blood, which does apply on the nights of יום טוב?
steps.whatsHappening: A second attack on רבי יוסי's קל וחומר. This one shows that מילה is not 'stronger' than covering in every way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if the source case is stronger in every relevant way. מילה is done only by day, while covering applies day and night. So covering has a strength that מילה lacks, and maybe its doubtful case does override יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What about X, which is special because...': the standard way to break a קל וחומר

steps.whatToRemember: רבה rejected רב עינא using רבי יוסי's ruling about a כוי, since its reasoning assumes covering never overrides שבת. The קל וחומר itself was then challenged twice: by the שופר counterexample, and by רבי אלעזר הקפר's point that מילה is done only by day.

phrases.aramaic: הֵשִׁיב רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הַקַּפָּר בְּרִיבִּי תְּשׁוּבָה:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar HaKappar the distinguished responded with a refutation:
What about circumcision?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן אֵינָהּ נוֹהֶגֶת בְּלֵילֵי יָמִים טוֹבִים,
phrases.english: It is special because it is not in effect on Festival nights,
Will you say the same about covering the blood,
which is in effect on Festival nights?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵשִׁיב רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הַקַּפָּר בְּרִיבִּי תְּשׁוּבָה מָה לְמִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different refutation of the קל וחומר in step 12, alongside the שופר attack in step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between מילה and covering the blood.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: מילה is weaker than covering in one way, since it does not apply at night, so it cannot serve as the stronger source for a קל וחומר.

steps.title: רבי אבא praises רבי אלעזר הקפר's answer
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא says that רבי יוסי's קל וחומר was one of the arguments רבי חייא said he could not refute, and רבי אלעזר הקפר did refute it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: This is one of the arguments about which רבי חייא said, 'I have no answer against them.' And רבי אלעזר הקפר, the great man, gave an answer.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא adds a side comment about the argument we just saw. רבי יוסי's קל וחומר was so strong that רבי חייא could not knock it down, but רבי אלעזר הקפר found a way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line does not add a new rule. It tells us how strong רבי יוסי's קל וחומר was, and that the successful attack on it is the one from Step 14 (מילה is not done on יום טוב nights). It closes the discussion of the קל וחומר before the גמרא returns to רבה's challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation, an answer that knocks down an argument
I have no refutation against them; I cannot disprove these arguments

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said:
This is one of the matters
phrases.notes: "This" is רבי יוסי's קל וחומר from Step 12.

phrases.english: about which Rabbi Chiya said
"I have no refutation against them,"

phrases.aramaic: וְהֵשִׁיב רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הַקַּפָּר בְּרִיבִּי תְּשׁוּבָה.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Elazar HaKappar, the great one, gave a refutation.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה אֶחָד מִן הַדְּבָרִים שֶׁאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on רבי אלעזר הקפר's refutation in Step 14 and confirms that it succeeds.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי's קל וחומר was one רבי חייא could not refute, but רבי אלעזר הקפר refuted it.

steps.title: The ברייתא still shows covering does not override שבת for a sick person
steps.stepSummary: Even with the קל וחומר set aside, the ברייתא assumes that a certain כיסוי does not push aside שבת. That must mean slaughtering for a sick person, which goes against רב עינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, the ברייתא teaches that a certain covering does not push aside שבת. What is a certain covering that does not push aside שבת? Is it not someone who slaughters for a sick person on שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבה's attack on רב עינא. Whether or not רבי יוסי's proof works, the ברייתא takes it for granted that a certain כיסוי does not push aside שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה is not relying on the קל וחומר itself, which was refuted. He is relying on its starting assumption: 'a certain כיסוי does not push aside שבת.' The only case where a certain obligation to cover comes up on שבת is permitted slaughter for a חולה. So the ברייתא says not to cover, which is the opposite of what רב עינא taught.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, it teaches. The גמרא uses this to pull a point from a source even after other parts of it were rejected.
Its certain case, when the obligation definitely applies
Pushes aside, or overrides, the laws of שבת
Covering the blood of a slaughtered bird or wild animal
A sick person, here one for whom slaughtering on שבת is permitted

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי's קל וחומר was refuted, but that does not cancel רבה's challenge. רבה only needs the starting fact the ברייתא assumes, not the conclusion it tried to prove.

phrases.english: In any case, it teaches,
covering, whose certain case does not push aside Shabbat.
What is a certain case of covering
that does not push aside Shabbat?
Is it not one who slaughters for a sick person on Shabbat?
phrases.notes: That is exactly רב עינא's case from Step 10, so the ברייתא seems to argue with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the debate over the קל וחומר and returns to רבה's challenge against רב עינא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב עינא's ruling that one covers the blood after slaughtering for a sick person on שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא assumes that a certain כיסוי does not override שבת. The only realistic certain case is slaughter for a חולה, so the ברייתא rules against covering in רב עינא's exact case.

steps.title: Maybe the ברייתא means someone who slaughtered against the law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the ברייתא's 'certain כיסוי' could be a case where someone broke שבת and slaughtered for no good reason. Then it would not be talking about a sick person at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps it is talking about one who sinned and slaughtered?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to defend רב עינא. Maybe the ברייתא is talking about someone who slaughtered on שבת when he was not allowed to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the slaughter itself was forbidden, it makes sense that we would not do another forbidden act to cover the blood. Slaughter for a sick person is permitted, so covering the blood there might still be required, as רב עינא said. This would remove the contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps; the גמרא uses this to suggest another way to read a source
He sinned, he did something that was not allowed

phrases.english: But perhaps it is where he sinned and slaughtered?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on Step 16 by offering a different case for the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the inference that the ברייתא's case must be slaughter for a sick person
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא's case could just as well be forbidden slaughter, so it need not be talking about רב עינא's case.

steps.title: Like circumcision, the slaughter must have been permitted
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא compares כיסוי to מילה, and מילה on שבת is done with permission. So the ברייתא's כיסוי must also follow a permitted slaughter, which means a sick person. The challenge to רב עינא stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is similar to circumcision. Just as circumcision is done with permission, so too covering is done with permission.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion in Step 17. Since רבי יוסי set כיסוי side by side with מילה, the two cases must match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מילה on the eighth day is a permitted, even required, act on שבת. For the comparison to work, the כיסוי case must also come after a permitted act, meaning slaughter for a חולה, not forbidden slaughter. So the ברייתא really does say not to cover in רב עינא's case, and רבה's challenge holds.

keyTerms.meaning: Similar to, matching. A case is read to fit the case it is compared with.
Circumcision, which on the eighth day is done even on שבת
With permission; done in a way the law allows

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי's קל וחומר was refuted, but the ברייתא still teaches that a certain כיסוי does not override שבת. Because it is compared to מילה, that means a permitted slaughter for a sick person. This stands as a challenge to רב עינא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common גמרא method: when a source places two cases side by side, we read the less clear case to match the clearer one (דומיא).

phrases.english: It is similar to circumcision:
just as circumcision is done with permission,
so too covering is also with permission.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 17's suggestion and puts Step 16's challenge back in place.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading a case to match the case it is compared with (דומיא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא might be talking about forbidden slaughter, which would leave רב עינא untouched.
steps.terutzMaskana: The comparison to מילה shows the slaughter was permitted, meaning for a sick person. So the ברייתא contradicts רב עינא.

steps.title: The Sages point to shofar as a proving case
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer רבי יוסי with the case of תקיעת שופר outside the מקדש. Its certain obligation does not push aside שבת, yet its doubtful obligation pushes aside יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: blowing שופר outside the מקדש will prove it. When it is definitely required, it does not push aside שבת, but when it is only doubtfully required, it does push aside יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back and quotes again the חכמים' answer from the ברייתא (seen in step 13), where blowing שופר 'proves' that רבי יוסי's קל וחומר does not hold. It quotes the line again in order to analyze it in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שופר is a מצוה that is never blown on שבת outside the מקדש, even when the obligation is certain. Yet a doubtful obligation to blow it is enough to push aside יום טוב. The חכמים use this pattern to show that רבי יוסי's link between certain and doubtful cases, and between שבת and יום טוב, is not a fixed rule.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Will prove': a formula that brings a counter-example to break an argument
Blowing the שופר on ראש השנה

phrases.english: They said to him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רבי יוסי, whose קל וחומר is being discussed.

phrases.english: The blowing of the shofar in the outlying areas will prove it,
phrases.notes: Outside the מקדש, the שופר was not blown when ראש השנה fell on שבת.

phrases.english: since its definite obligation does not push aside Shabbat,
and its doubtful obligation does push aside Yom Tov.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: תְּקִיעַת שׁוֹפָר בַּגְּבוּלִין תּוֹכִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the wording of the ברייתא's debate with רבי יוסי and quotes again the שופר proving case from step 13 so it can be analyzed.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי יוסי's קל וחומר about כיסוי
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case of שופר shows that a doubtful obligation can push aside יום טוב even though the certain obligation does not push aside שבת. So the pattern the argument relies on does not always hold.

steps.title: What is the doubtful case of shofar?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא means by a 'doubtful' obligation of שופר that pushes aside יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is its doubtful case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask a clarifying question about the חכמים' words. This sets up the next move, where it tests possible answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proving case only works if we know what kind of doubt is meant. The גמרא wants to find a doubt that actually fits the debate about כיסוי הדם on יום טוב.

phrases.english: What is its doubtful case?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a term used in the proving case from step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of doubt about שופר pushes aside יום טוב.

steps.title: It cannot mean a doubt about whether the day is יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the doubt is whether the day is a weekday or יום טוב. It rejects this, because if שופר pushes aside a definite יום טוב, it obviously pushes aside a doubtful one.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the doubt is whether the day is a weekday or יום טוב: now, a definite יום טוב it pushes aside, so does it even need to be said about a day that might be יום טוב or might be a weekday?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a first answer to its question and immediately knocks it down as too obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blowing שופר is the main מצוה of ראש השנה, which is a definite יום טוב. So it certainly may be done on a day that is only maybe יום טוב. Saying so would teach nothing new, and it would not compare to כיסוי on a definite יום טוב, so the גמרא must look for a different kind of doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If you say': introduces a suggestion that will be rejected
'Now': opens a 'how much more so' argument
'Is it even needed?': this would be too obvious to teach

phrases.aramaic: אִילֵּימָא סָפֵק חוֹל סָפֵק יוֹם טוֹב –
phrases.english: If you say: a doubt whether it is a weekday or Yom Tov,
now, a definite Yom Tov it pushes aside,

phrases.aramaic: סָפֵק יוֹם טוֹב סָפֵק חוֹל מִיבַּעְיָא?
phrases.english: does a doubtful Yom Tov, doubtful weekday, even need to be said?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא סָפֵק חוֹל סָפֵק יוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first possible answer to the question in step 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that 'its doubt' means a doubt whether the day is a weekday or יום טוב
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: If שופר pushes aside a definite יום טוב, it obviously pushes aside a doubtful one. The ruling would be pointless and would not fit the comparison to כיסוי.
